newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy opposition head sees "desire" for EMU delay.
newsitem.headline: Italy opposition head sees "desire" for EMU delay.

text.p: Italian opposition leader Silvio Berlusconi said on Tuesday he believed there was now "a desire to delay" the launch of the European single currency in the wake of France's request for more time to study the stability pact.
"There's a great deal of confusion," the centre-right opposition leader told reporters when asked about the French move.
The stability pact, which is designed to enforce fiscal restraint in EMU member states, was due to be signed at the forthcoming Amsterdam summit of European Union heads of state.
Berlusconi, who was Italian prime minister in 1994, said his own position on European economic and monetary union (EMU), was now being proved right.

"(I said) that either we should have a delay to the start date for monetary union or else a more flexible interpretation of the criteria. Even on this we are now seen to be correct, as on everything else," he said.

Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi has repeatedly said there should be no delay to the launch of the single currency, set for January 1999, and has said he will not seek any softening of the economic criteria set for EMU aspirants. -- Rome newsroom +396 6782501
